learningObjectives: Add Test Configuration Parameters to API TestStepValues, such as a shared Service Access Key.
Jump between a TestStep and its underlying Module using CTRL+J or the context menu.
Use the F9 toggle to hide empty values in long API TestCases.
Refresh Modules and TestCases directly from the API Scan after the server or API structure changes.

elements.text: Worked example: add a new coffee shop branch, verify it was added, then delete it — the same three-step pattern (Create → Verify → Delete) introduced in the previous lesson, now fully wired up with real values and run end-to-end.
Official Best Practice: when Modules are updated in Tosca Commander, the TestStep will automatically be updated.

elements.description: As with UI automation, when a Module is updated in Tosca Commander, its linked TestStep — and by extension the whole TestCase — updates automatically. If you're unsure which Module a TestStep links to, select the TestStep and press Ctrl+J, or right-click it and choose "Jump to Module".

elements.term: Adding Modules to an API TestCase
elements.description: Like in UI TestCases, Modules can be added to an API TestCase either by dragging and dropping them from the Modules section, or with the Ctrl+T shortcut — both methods work identically to how you already add Modules in UI automation.

elements.term: Test Configuration Parameters (TCP) in API TestCases
elements.description: Just like in UI TestCases, add a Test Configuration Parameter — e.g. "Key" holding the Service Access Key — to every TestStepValue that needs it. This is far less laborious than updating the same literal value in every TestStep individually if the key ever changes, especially in long TestCases.

elements.text: Buffering the ID from a Create step lets the Constraint ActionMode identify that exact new shop later (to Verify its name/city/country), and the same buffered ID is reused again in the Delete TestStep.

bulletPoints: A fully populated API TestCase is just as business-readable as a UI TestCase — an entry-level Automation Specialist with no programming/API knowledge can follow and run it.
F9 toggles hiding TestStepValues with no value set — invaluable for long, wide API TestCases.
The Control Flow Diagram gives the same visual TestCase overview you already know from UI automation.
Run in the Scratchbook, then set WorkState to Completed once the TestCase runs cleanly start-to-finish.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Updating Modules and TestCases from the API Scan

elements.title: Pushing many server-side changes back into Tosca at once
items: In Tosca Commander, select the Module(s) that need updating — for a Request+Response pair, select both, or select their containing folder.
On the ribbon, open API Testing > the dropdown below the API Scan button > "Open Selected Modules" to reload them inside the API Scan itself.
Make the necessary changes inside the API Scan.
Click "Update" in the ribbon — the Modules and TestCases back in Tosca Commander are refreshed to match.

elements.text: Official Best Practice: when updating Modules, both the Request and the Response need to be selected, in order to update both.

bulletPoints: This is the API-Scan-side counterpart to the manual "Update" from the Technical View covered in the previous lesson — use whichever is more convenient for the scale of the change.

elements.title: Key Points (verbatim from the course's end-of-lesson summary slides):
items: When Modules are updated in Tosca Commander, the TestStep will automatically be updated.
Like in UI TestCases, Modules can be added by dragging and dropping them or with the Ctrl+T shortcut.
When updating Modules, both the Request and the Response need to be selected, in order to update both.

elements.text: These 3 points are the official Lesson 7 recap — treat them as something you must be able to recall word-for-word for the exam.

examPitfalls.title: Not knowing how to jump from a TestStep to its Module
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates manually search through the Modules folder to find which one a given TestStep is linked to.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Select the TestStep and press Ctrl+J, or right-click it and choose "Jump to Module", to navigate there directly.

examPitfalls.title: Hardcoding a shared value like the Service Access Key everywhere
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates type the same Service Access Key literally into every TestStepValue that needs it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add it once as a Test Configuration Parameter (e.g. "Key") and reference it everywhere — updating it in one place if it ever changes, instead of hunting through every TestStep.

examPitfalls.title: Only selecting one side of a Module pair before updating from the API Scan
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates select only the Request Module (or only the Response Module) before clicking Update, leaving the other half stale.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Select BOTH the Request and Response Modules (or their containing folder) before updating from the API Scan, so both halves refresh together.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking API TestCases need a special way to add Modules
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume API TestCases require a different, API-specific method for adding a Module as a TestStep.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Official course Best Practice: like in UI TestCases, Modules can be added to an API TestCase by dragging and dropping them, or with the Ctrl+T shortcut — no new mechanism to learn.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to quickly find which Module a specific TestStep in an API TestCase is linked to. What is the fastest way?

options.text: Manually browse the entire Modules folder until the right one is found.
Select the TestStep and press Ctrl+J, or right-click it and choose "Jump to Module".
Delete the TestStep and re-add it from scratch.
This information cannot be determined once imported.

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a direct keyboard shortcut for this, plus a context-menu equivalent.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+J (or right-click > "Jump to Module") instantly navigates from a selected TestStep to its linked Module — no manual searching required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A long API TestCase has many TestStepValues, most of them empty. What toggle makes the TestCase easier to read by hiding the empty ones?

options.text: F6
F2
F9
Ctrl+T

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the same key used in AS1/AS2 for hiding empty TestStepValues.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Toggling F9 hides TestStepValues that have no value set, which is especially useful for long, wide API TestCases with many optional fields.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The underlying API structure has changed in several places at once. What is the correct sequence to refresh the already-imported Modules and TestCases in Tosca?

options.text: Delete the old Modules and manually recreate them from scratch.
Select the Modules in Tosca Commander, open them in the API Scan via API Testing > "Open Selected Modules", make the changes, then click Update.
Simply re-save the Tosca project — changes sync automatically.
Rename the Modules; Tosca will detect the API changes on its own.

practiceQuiz.hint: This mirrors updating from the Technical View, but starts from inside the API Scan itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Select the Modules needing an update, use API Testing > the dropdown below the API Scan button > "Open Selected Modules" to load them in the API Scan, make the changes there, then click "Update" in the ribbon to refresh Tosca.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When updating both halves of a Message's Modules from the API Scan, what must be selected in Tosca Commander first?

options.text: Only the Response Module — the Request updates automatically.
Only the Request Module — the Response updates automatically.
Both the Request and Response Modules (or their containing folder).
The entire Component Folder for the whole project.

practiceQuiz.hint: Request and Response are independent Modules in Tosca — updating one does not touch the other.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Both the Request and Response Modules must be selected (or their containing folder, if both live there) in order to update both sides together from the API Scan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which methods can be used to add a Module as a TestStep in an API TestCase?

options.text: Only through the API Scan's own export button — Modules cannot be added manually afterward.
Dragging and dropping the Module, or using the Ctrl+T shortcut — the same methods used in UI TestCases.
Only by right-clicking and choosing "Insert API Module", a command unique to API TestCases.
API TestCases do not support adding Modules after the initial export.

practiceQuiz.hint: Nothing new here — it works exactly like UI TestCases.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Official Key Point: like in UI TestCases, Modules can be added by dragging and dropping them, or with the Ctrl+T shortcut. API TestCases don't require a separate, special mechanism.

Drag and drop, or Ctrl+T — the same two methods as UI TestCases.
